dives: Why local-first for an inbox?
Reading from IndexedDB means the first paint needs no network, so the inbox opens instantly and works offline. The network only brings changes, and the UI updates when they arrive.
How does delta sync work?

Store the last history id. Ask for changes since it, apply them to the local database, and save the new id. If the server says the id is too old (Gmail keeps history at least a week), do a full re-sync.
How do you render untrusted email HTML safely?

Sanitise it, put it in an iframe with the sandbox attribute (no scripts), use srcdoc and a strict CSP, block remote images by default to stop tracking, and never combine allow-scripts with allow-same-origin because that undoes the sandbox.
How does undo send work?
Do not send at once: put the message in the outbox with a delay of a few seconds (Gmail offers 5 to 30). Undo removes it; otherwise it sends with an idempotency key so retries cannot duplicate it.
How do you scroll a huge mailbox smoothly?
Virtualize the list so only the visible rows plus a small overscan are in the DOM, use fixed or estimated row heights, and page metadata in batches while bodies load later.
How does search work offline?
Build a token index on the device in a Web Worker (tokenise, case-fold, prefix match) over downloaded messages, show local hits at once, and merge server results for older mail.
Several tabs open?
Elect a leader tab with the Web Locks API so only one tab syncs, share changes through BroadcastChannel and keep IndexedDB as the single store.
Accessibility of the list?
Use a listbox or grid pattern with one tab stop and arrow-key movement, announce unread state and selection, keep shortcuts discoverable and switchable, and provide focus after archive or delete.

dives: Why canvas and not a table of divs?

A big visible grid in DOM means thousands of nodes and slow style and layout work. A canvas redraws just the visible cells directly. Google moved Docs to canvas rendering for performance and consistency, and the same reasoning applies to grids.
How does virtualization work in two directions?

Compute the first and last visible row and column from scroll offsets and cumulative row heights and column widths, then draw only those plus overscan. Keep a prefix-sum (or tree) of sizes so mapping offset to index is fast even with custom sizes.
How are formulas recalculated efficiently?

Parse into a dependency graph. When a cell changes, mark it dirty, walk its dependents in topological order, recompute only those, detect cycles, and send the changed values back in one batch. Run it in a Web Worker so typing stays smooth.
How do you stay accessible if the grid is canvas?

Mirror the active area in a hidden DOM grid with role grid, row and gridcell, and aria-rowcount, aria-colcount, aria-rowindex and aria-colindex for the full size. Follow the WAI-ARIA grid keyboard pattern: arrows, Home and End, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End, Page Up and Down.
How do you keep text input and IME right?
Do not draw an editor yourself. Overlay a real input or contenteditable on the active cell so IME, spellcheck, paste and screen readers work.
How is collaboration handled?

Send small operations ('set cell A1 to 5') with a base revision. The server orders them; conflicting edits to the same cell are decided by order (last writer wins) which is fine for cells. Structural changes like inserting a row need transformation or a CRDT for position.
How do undo and redo fit in?
Each action is a command object with do and undo. Undo applies the inverse and sends it as a normal operation, so everyone stays consistent; keep one stack per user.
Loading a huge sheet?
Fetch only the visible window and a margin from the server, show placeholders while scrolling fast, cancel stale requests, and cache fetched blocks in memory.

dives: Why put filters in the URL?

The URL becomes the single source of truth: shareable links, working back and forward buttons, refresh keeps state, and SSR can render the right page. Components read from the URL and update it, rather than keeping separate state.
How do list and map stay in sync?

Both read the same cached result set. Hovering a card sets an activeId that highlights the pin and the reverse, and the map's moveend event (debounced) updates the bbox in the URL, which triggers a new fetch.
How do you stop the map from spamming the API?
Debounce map moves, fetch only on moveend not on every frame, cancel in-flight requests with AbortController, and show a 'Search this area' button if auto-search is too noisy.
How do you prevent a double booking or double charge?

Generate an idempotency key (a UUID) when the checkout opens and send it on the booking POST. Disable the button while pending. A retry after a timeout returns the saved result instead of creating a second booking.
Server rendering or client rendering for search?
Server-render the first results for SEO and fast LCP, then hydrate. Later filter changes can be client-side navigations that fetch JSON, with the URL updated and results cached.
How do you make the date picker accessible and international?
Use a grid with arrow-key navigation, labels per day, clear blocked-date states and range announcements; format with Intl.DateTimeFormat, respect the locale's first day of the week, and support RTL.
How do you keep payment data safe?

Use the payment provider's hosted fields in an iframe, load their script from their origin, add a CSP, and send only a token to our server. Auth uses an HttpOnly SameSite cookie, with CSRF protection on state-changing calls.
How do you avoid layout shift and slow images?

Reserve image space with width and height or aspect-ratio, serve responsive sizes and modern formats, give the first image priority, lazy-load the rest and keep skeletons the same size as final cards.

dives: The user taps Withdraw, the network drops, they tap again. What happens?
The same idempotency key is reused for that withdraw, so the server returns the first result instead of paying twice. The button disables while a request is in flight.
Optimistic UI for a withdrawal?
No. Show a pending state and wait for the server. Optimistic is fine for likes, not for money.
How do you store and show money?
Integer minor units plus currency code; format with Intl.NumberFormat for the user's locale; never use floats for amounts.
How do you make it fast on a cheap Android phone?
Small first route, lazy everything else, avoid big libraries, cut re-renders (OnPush / signals or memo), virtualize long lists, measure INP and startup on a real low-end device.
Patchy network: what does the user see?
Cached balance with its time, a clear offline banner, queued actions marked pending, and retry with backoff when back online.
Where do tokens live in a hybrid app?
In secure native storage through a plugin, not localStorage; short-lived access token, refresh handled carefully, lock after inactivity.
How do you ship a fix without a store release?
Live updates of the web bundle on a channel, behind flags, with a minimum native version check for anything that needs new native code.
How do you roll out per country?
Remote config per country (limits, copy, features) with safe defaults cached on device and kill switches for risky flows.
wrap: Bottleneck: payday spikes and flaky networks. Fix: cached reads, idempotent writes, push instead of polling.
Next: offline-safe history, accessibility audit on real devices, and an INP budget in CI.

dives: Client-side or server-side table?
Server-side sort, filter and paging once data is large; client-side is fine for a few hundred rows.
Two admins edit the same row. What happens?
Send a version with the update; the server returns 409 on conflict and the UI shows the newer data to merge.
How do you keep a 10,000-row CSV upload smooth?
Parse and validate in a Web Worker, show the first errors with row numbers, then upload and run the import as a job.
Roles in the frontend?
Hide or disable actions the role cannot use for clarity, but the server is the real check.
How do you make the table accessible?
Real table semantics or the ARIA grid pattern, sortable headers announced with aria-sort, keyboard navigation and visible focus.

Sort, filters and page in the URL, so the back button and links work.

reqF: Tenants start agent runs through an API, chat channels or a schedule, and stream progress live
A run can last 30+ minutes, with tens of model calls, tool calls and code runs
If a worker crashes or is redeployed, the run carries on from its last step on another worker
Agents run untrusted, model-written code safely
Tenants set budgets; a run stops cleanly when it hits its cap
Engineers can open any run, see every step and replay it from any point
reqN: Isolation: no tenant can see another tenant's data, code, secrets or tools
Durability: no run is lost on a crash or deploy; each step happens once from the user's view
Fairness: one tenant's burst can't starve the others
Cost control: spend is metered per call and enforced before the next call
Observability: every step is traced with tokens, cost, latency and errors
est: Assume 2k tenants, 500k runs/day, peak ~20 runs/s starting
Average run ~10 min -> ~20 x 600 s = ~12k runs in flight at peak -> long-lived leases on a worker pool, not request threads
~40 steps per run, checkpoint ~50 KB each -> ~2 MB per run, ~1 TB/day -> keep the last steps hot, move finished runs to cheap storage
~30% of runs execute code -> ~4k sandboxes alive at peak; a microVM boots in ~125 ms, so start on demand and keep a small warm pool
Traces: ~40 spans per run -> ~20M spans/day; sample content, keep metadata for every span

checkpoints (run_id, step, state blob, created_at) - append only
steps / spans (run_id, step, kind: model | tool | code, tokens, cost, latency, error)

blocks.cl: Runs start from the API, a chat channel or a schedule; all of them become the same run request.
blocks.ctl: The control plane authenticates the tenant, applies limits and writes the run row before anything runs.
blocks.ts: Every model call, tool call and code run is a span. You can open a run, step through it and replay from any checkpoint.
blocks.sp: Before each model call the meter checks what this run and tenant have spent; at the cap the run pauses or stops cleanly.
blocks.q: A queue with a lane per tenant and concurrency caps, so one tenant's burst waits its turn.
blocks.w: Workers lease a run, run the agent loop and renew the lease with heartbeats. If a worker dies, the lease expires and another worker takes over.
blocks.ck: State is saved after every step, so a new worker resumes from the last step, not from the start.
blocks.gw: Every model call goes through one gateway: routing, retries, fallbacks and token counts for the meter.
blocks.llm: The models doing the thinking, usually a mix of large and small ones.
blocks.sbx: Model-written code runs in a fresh microVM per run, with no secrets and only the network it needs.
blocks.mg: Tool calls go through an MCP gateway that checks the tenant's grants, swaps in the right token and logs every call.
blocks.mcp: The tools themselves: search, CRM, code hosts, internal APIs, each behind MCP.

dives: A worker crashes 20 minutes into a run. What happens?

The worker held a lease with a heartbeat. The heartbeat stops, the lease expires, and the run goes back on the queue. Another worker loads the last checkpoint and carries on. Steps with side effects carry an idempotency key, so a step that was half done is not done twice.
How do you isolate untrusted code from many tenants?

One sandbox per run, never shared across tenants. Containers share the host kernel, so for untrusted code use a microVM (Firecracker: its own guest kernel, boots in about 125 ms) or a user-space kernel like gVisor. No secrets inside, egress through an allowlist proxy, CPU, memory and time limits, and the sandbox is destroyed when the run ends.
How do you enforce a budget when cost is only known after the call?

Meter every call at the gateway and keep a running total per run and per tenant. Before each call, check spent plus a worst-case estimate (max output tokens x price) against the cap. Hard cap: stop or pause the run with a clear status. Soft cap: alert the tenant. Reconcile with the provider's usage later.
How do tools stay safe when agents call them for many tenants?

All tool calls go through an MCP gateway. It checks which tools this tenant and agent may use, swaps in a token issued for that server (never passes the user's token through), and logs every call. With the 2026-07-28 MCP spec the gateway can route on the Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers without reading the body.
How do you debug a run that went wrong yesterday?

Open its trace: every step is a span with inputs, outputs, tokens and cost (OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions make them portable). Load the checkpoint before the bad step, change the prompt or tool, and replay from there in a sandbox. Turn the failure into an eval case.
How do you keep the platform fair under a burst?
Per-tenant queues with weighted fair scheduling, max concurrent runs per tenant, token rate limits at the gateway, and priority lanes for interactive runs over batch ones.
